findings.title: Exposed .env with application secrets
findings.evidence: HTTP 200, text/plain, KEY=VALUE lines including a database URL; value redacted
findings.impact: An anonymous visitor could obtain backend and integration credentials for this environment.
findings.remediation: Remove the file from the web root, rotate every secret it contained, and add a deploy check that blocks dotfiles.
findings.limits: The file was fingerprinted only; values were not used or stored.

findings.title: Exposed Git metadata
findings.impact: Repository structure and possibly full history may be recoverable by an anonymous visitor.
findings.remediation: Block /.git/ at the web server and rebuild the deployment without VCS metadata.
findings.limits: Objects were not downloaded; no reconstruction attempted.

findings.title: Spring Boot actuator reachable
findings.evidence: HTTP 200, JSON with propertySources keys; full body not retrieved
findings.impact: Environment property names may reveal internal service topology and configuration.
findings.remediation: Disable or authenticate actuator endpoints; expose only health at the edge.
findings.limits: No secret values were extracted; response confirmed by structure only.

findings.title: Public API schema
findings.evidence: HTTP 200, JSON with openapi and paths keys
findings.impact: Endpoint names and parameters are discoverable, which slightly reduces recon effort.
findings.remediation: Publish docs only where intended; keep internal schemas off the public host.
findings.limits: Documentation is public by design on many APIs; confirm intent before removing.
